about: Prompts written to sit OUTSIDE the stage C word lists (the fixed prompt_suite.json was written with that parser in mind). Same format as prompt_suite.json: expect = collapsed window classes in order (L left-turning, R right-turning, S straight and moving, X standing, U unspecified); forbid = classes that must not appear. IMPORTANT, learned the hard way: a parser that simply IGNORES unknown words already passes most prompts whose only unknown words are verbs, because it only needs the direction words. So the tiers that tell a word list from a model are meaning and directions: there the unknown words (or a known word used in another sense) carry the answer. Tiers: meaning = negation, contrast, stop synonyms, 'right' that is not a direction (the gate tier); directions = clockwise / port / starboard (the gate tier, hard); verbs and phrasing = unknown verbs and other sentence shapes with known direction words (a no-regression tier); distractor = text with no motion in it: the right answer is no plan or all-unspecified, any L / R / S / X window is an invented motion. Add your own: the more this set looks like how people really type, the better the comparison. NOTE: a dataset whose phrasings were all filtered by the stage C parser contains no negation or contrast, so a model trained on it may fail the meaning tier too: that failure is information about the data, not about the encoder.
